stem:
The diagram shows lines $LM$ and $NO$ cut by transversal $BD$. Lalit notes that triangles $LBD$ and $NDB$ are congruent, and that congruence makes a pair of alternate interior angles equal.

Which claim correctly concludes that $LM \parallel NO$?

options.text: $LM \parallel NO$, because the congruent triangles make a pair of alternate interior angles equal for transversal $BD$.
Lines $LM$ and $NO$ are the alternate interior angles on transversal $BD$.
$LM \parallel NO$, because the triangles are congruent, even when those alternate interior angles are unequal.
$LM \parallel NO$, because matching sides of the triangles are equal, and equal sides alone settle parallelism.

teacher.key_rationale: Equal alternate interior angles from the congruence force LM∥NO. Renaming the lines as the angles swaps terms. Dropping the equal-angle step, or treating equal sides alone as enough, misses the parallel hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source right triangle as lines LM and NO cut by transversal BD.
